gloss: hidden scoring cuts (made in food before cooking)

definitions.gloss: hidden knife cuts; scoring made on the underside of an ingredient
definitions.explanation: Shallow cuts made where they will not be seen on the finished dish, so that heat and seasoning penetrate faster and the piece is easier to eat. Standard practice with daikon, konnyaku, squid, and thick cuts of fish.

examples.japanese: {大根|だいこん}に{隠|かく}し{包丁|ぼうちょう}を{入|い}れる。
examples.english: Score the underside of the daikon.

examples.japanese: {隠|かく}し{包丁|ぼうちょう}を{入|い}れると{味|あじ}がしみやすくなる。
examples.english: Making hidden cuts helps the flavor soak in.

examples.japanese: {裏側|うらがわ}に{十字|じゅうじ}の{隠|かく}し{包丁|ぼうちょう}を{入|い}れておくと、{煮崩|にくず}れせずに{中|なか}まで{火|ひ}が{通|とお}る。
examples.english: If you cut a cross on the underside beforehand, it cooks through without falling apart.

notes:
Literally "hidden knife." Here {包丁|ぼうちょう} stands for the cut made with the knife, not the knife itself.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {隠|かく}し{包丁|ぼうちょう}を{入|い}れる: to make hidden cuts (the standard verb)
- {十字|じゅうじ}の{隠|かく}し{包丁|ぼうちょう}: a cross-shaped scoring cut
- {裏|うら}に{隠|かく}し{包丁|ぼうちょう}: cuts on the underside

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {飾|かざ}り{包丁|ぼうちょう}: decorative cuts — meant to be seen, for appearance
- {切|き}り{込|こ}み: a slit, an incision — the general word for a cut into something
